rationale: This is mechanically MIN(LiquidCurrentAssetProfit, NetWorkingCapitalClaimsProfit) — a conjunction of two already-tested archive signals whose realization legs (che/act and −netWC/at) are themselves strongly collinear, so it is a cosmetic recombination rather than a new characteristic, and the "fix" for the SUMRANK variant's dead FMB slope is asserted rather than economically diagnosed.

A defensible full-coverage balance-sheet analog of the archive's best-Sharpe accrual-per-claim leg that isolates deflator from data source, though it is close to a classic Sloan accrual measure in new clothing and the unwinsorized (act−che) denominator can blow up for cash-heavy or service firms.

The expression and negative expected sign are internally consistent (MIN isolates the high-profit/high-accrual corner) and the short-side symmetry test is a legitimate diagnostic, but it is largely the mirror image of the already-tested AccrualPerClaimDollarProfit and re-treads the well-known accrual anomaly at only ~8% coverage.

che/(act−che+lct) will be nearly rank-collinear with both che/act and che/lct, whose conjunctions with gross profitability already deliver ~5% alpha at t≈5, so this is a denominator tweak on a saturated leg rather than a differently-ordered characteristic, and the claim that it "orders firms differently" is unsupported.

The second-moment accrual-quality channel is genuinely under-tested in this archive, the net working capital stock is the theoretically right object versus the earlier gross-claims-to-sales attempt, and the construction is internally coherent — though the VOL leg risks proxying for firm-level volatility and size, which the eventual diagnosis should address.

Both legs are driven by the same oancf term (high oancf raises the cash margin and lowers ib−oancf), so the "conjunction" largely double-counts one variable rather than combining independent evidence, and it simply pairs two existing archive legs at the family's most restrictive coverage.
